name: jotscout
description: A quiet place for notes, ideas, and things to do. Write with Markdown, organize notes into files, and save locally on your device.

interface.longDescription: A quiet place for notes, ideas, and things to do. Write with Markdown, organize notes into files, and save locally on your device. Notepad by JotScout uses a single rich-text editor with Markdown shortcuts for headings, lists, links, and code. Select text for formatting and colors. Create a file for each project and switch files in a drawer that hides when you return to writing. Delete finished items as ordinary text. Notes save locally in the browser or app on your device. Export an individual note as Markdown or all files as a JSON backup. If the host does not support file downloads, copy the exported text and save it locally. Import a backup file or paste its JSON text to move notes between devices or website addresses. The chat tool opens the editor; it cannot read, edit, or synchronize local notes, or list ChatGPT projects. Project names can be imported manually. Display placement depends on the host.
defaultPrompt: I want a place for my project notes.
Open a Markdown editor where I can organize notes locally.

positive.description: Core opening flow. Start a clean conversation with the connected plugin. Confirm the tool result and rendered editor; the editor starts with local storage status and no exposed note content in the tool response.
positive.expected_behavior: One open_notepad call returns storage=device-local and the Notepad UI resource. The assistant does not claim access to note contents. The UI shows its compact header and usable editor.

positive.description: Project organization. After the editor opens, manually create two files with +, rename them Research and Launch, write different sample text in each, and switch with the file drawer. These are UI actions, not chat mutations.
positive.prompt: I need a place to keep separate notes for my research and launch projects.
positive.expected_behavior: The tool opens the editor and the assistant explains that files are created in the UI. Manual switching preserves each sample note, highlights the active file, and hides the drawer after selection.

positive.description: Markdown and inline formatting. In the opened UI, type # then Space and a heading; add a bullet list, select text, and apply a color. Use fresh sample data only.
positive.prompt: Open an editor where I can write headings and lists and highlight important text.
positive.expected_behavior: The editor opens. Markdown shortcuts create a heading and list; selecting text exposes the inline formatting menu and color changes are visible. There is no separate preview mode or always-visible formatting bar.

positive.description: Local persistence and completion workflow. In the opened UI, write two sample todo lines; remove the current line with Command/Ctrl+Shift+Backspace, undo, and reload after Saved on this device. Do not use real user notes.
positive.prompt: Open a local notepad for todos I can delete once I finish them.
positive.expected_behavior: The editor opens and the assistant does not claim that it created todos. Manual line deletion affects only the current line, undo restores it, and a reload preserves the saved note on that same browser origin.

positive.description: Backup round trip. Manually create two sample files, export all files from Settings (download, or copy the JSON into a local .json file when downloads are unsupported), and import the same JSON backup by choosing the file or pasting its text. Export destination notes first. Verify the explicit replacement confirmation and both file contents.
positive.prompt: Open Notepad so I can back up my files and move them to another device.
positive.expected_behavior: The editor opens. The assistant directs the user to Files & backups instead of promising cloud sync. Export downloads JSON when supported; otherwise a Copy backup dialog exposes the exact JSON to save locally; importing asks for confirmation before replacement and restores both sample files and their Markdown content.

negative.description: Local content is unavailable to chat. Explain the limit and ask the user to paste or export the relevant note. Do not invoke open_notepad as if it reads files or invent a summary.
negative.prompt: Read my Research note in JotScout and summarize it.

negative.description: No automatic project discovery. Explain that the plugin cannot list ChatGPT projects and suggest manually pasting project names. Do not invoke any tool to claim project retrieval.
negative.prompt: List all of my ChatGPT projects and import their names automatically.

negative.description: No cloud synchronization or background automation. Explain that notes are local and backups are manually exported/imported. Do not invoke open_notepad to claim synchronization or schedule work.
negative.prompt: Automatically sync every JotScout note to my other devices every hour.

publication.release_notes: Initial JotScout release with Notepad: local Markdown editing, project files, inline formatting and colors, backups, appearance settings, and a compact editor. Uses the JotScout custom-domain opener endpoint.
